effects.target: Reshapes one subject with Shadow Plane energy, duplicating any one of animal growth, anthropomorphic animal, enlarge person, fins to feet, longarm, polymorph, reduce person or stone fist; the subject gains no sensory abilities of the new form and no movement speed above its own base. Any creature interacting with the subject may attempt a Will save to disbelieve; a creature that succeeds takes one-fifth (20%) damage from the shadowy form's natural attacks and special abilities, and the form's non-damaging abilities have only a 20% chance of working on it.

shadow-transmutation.notes: Range, target and duration are all 'see text' because they are taken from whichever spell is mimicked - nothing to structure, so duration is omitted rather than guessed. The 20% figure is a damage *reduction* applied to the subject's own attacks against disbelievers, not damage the spell deals, so it is not a damage spec.

effects.target: As shadow transmutation, but it can duplicate greater polymorph as well. The shadowy form's illusory attacks and special abilities deal three-fifths (60%) damage to creatures that disbelieved, and its non-damaging effects are 60% likely to work on them.

shadow-transmutation-greater.notes: Duration 'see text'; omitted. 60% is a fraction of the subject's own attack damage, not spell damage.

effects.target: The target's shadow is pinned where it stands: while entangled this way it cannot move more than 5 feet from its original position, and a flying creature can only hover or fall. On each of its turns the target may attempt a new save as a full-round action to end the effect. The spell fails automatically against a creature that casts no shadow, and ends if the target is in an area of no illumination at all.

shadow-trap.notes: Entangled is stated outright ('causing the target to become entangled'). The 5-foot leash, the repeat save and the no-shadow/no-light exclusions have no vocabulary, so they are narrated beside it.

effects.target: You and any creatures you touch (one per caster level, all touching one another) step onto the border of the Plane of Shadow and travel at 50 miles per hour relative to the Material Plane, stepping back off wherever you choose. Terrain cannot be made out in transit, so it is useless for scouting. When the spell ends you are shunted 1d10 x 100 feet in a random horizontal direction from the intended endpoint. It can also reach other planes bordering the Plane of Shadow; that transit takes 1d4 hours. An unwilling creature gets a Will save to avoid being taken along.

shadow-walk.notes: The fatigue ('renders each creature fatigued (no save)') is NOT converted to apply_condition: it happens only in the second-order failure branch where two successive random shunts both land inside solid matter. Converting it would fatigue every traveller on every casting. Likewise the 1d10 figures are displacement in feet, not damage.

effects.target: Shapes a quasi-real masterwork melee weapon of any type you are proficient with; you attack with it as a real weapon and it deals that weapon type's normal damage. The first creature it hits may attempt a Will save to disbelieve - on a success the weapon deals it only 1 point of damage per hit thereafter. It deals only 1 point of damage to objects. Against a creature with spell resistance you make a caster level check the first time the weapon strikes it; if the weapon is resisted the spell is dispelled. At caster level 5th the weapon gains a +1 enhancement bonus; at 10th you may make that +2 or instead add the frost or keen property, neither of which works on a creature that disbelieved. The spell ends if the weapon leaves your possession.

shadow-weapon.notes: No damage spec: the damage is the conjured weapon's own ('normal damage for a weapon of its type'), which the brief excludes, and the type is chosen at casting. The +1/+2 enhancement bonus is real but gated on caster level 5 and 10, and the schema has no level-gated modifier - emitting a flat +1 would be wrong for a 3rd-level caster, so it is narrated.

effects.target: Conjures a quasi-real shadowy duplicate of yourself that follows you automatically, even through teleportation, and cannot be damaged though it can be dispelled. It begins a bardic performance of your choice from among those you know and continues it until you spend a move action to switch. Its rounds of performance do not draw on your own daily rounds, and it cannot trigger spells keyed to your beginning or ending a performance.

shadowbard.notes: Summons an effect that performs; nothing in the vocabulary summons or performs.

effects.target: In areas of darkness the target is invisible to creatures relying on darkvision; in dim light it has concealment against them. No effect in normal light or brighter, and the spell is dispelled automatically if the target enters bright light or takes a hostile action.

shadowfade.notes: The vocabulary has no invisibility or concealment effect, and this one is conditional on both the ambient light and the observer's sense - a condition the schema cannot express at all.

effects.target: The target's body becomes quasi-real shadow. A foe trying to attack it directly (weapon or targeted spell) must make a Will save to disbelieve; on a success that foe attacks normally and ignores the spell for 1 round, and on a failure the target takes only one-fifth the damage from that attack, with any non-damage rider one-fifth as strong or only 20% likely to occur. Objects automatically succeed at this save.

shadowform.notes: Fractional incoming-damage reduction keyed to a per-attacker save. damage_reduction is a flat subtraction, not a fraction, so using it would be a different rule with a made-up number.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The creature perceives the world around it as one light level darker than it truly is. This is an illusion of darkness, not darkness: the real light level is unchanged, low-light vision and darkvision do not see through it, and even a creature that sees through magical darkness loses vision to it.

shadowmind.notes: One target per caster level, none more than 30 feet apart. The effect is a perceived light level, which the vocabulary has no term for - dazzled is a different rule and would have been an invented one.

effects.target: As rope trick, but entered through a touched 5-foot square of floor or wall. Creates an extradimensional space adjacent to the Plane of Shadow holding up to 10 creatures of any size, hidden from spells and divinations that do not work across planes. Neither spells nor area effects cross the interface; those inside can see out through an invisible 5-foot window that cannot be seen through from outside. The entrance shows as an area darker than its surroundings and is open only while the light around it is dim - any brighter or darker level closes it and traps those inside. Everything inside is ejected when the spell ends; if the entrance was closed at that moment there is a 50% chance the occupants are instead ejected onto the Shadow Plane, 1d10 miles in a random direction from the corresponding spot. No effect on a plane not adjacent to the Shadow Plane. Shadow walk and similar travel to the Shadow Plane arrives at half the usual off-target distance from this space.

shadowy-haven.notes: 1d10 here is miles of displacement on a 50% ejection branch, not damage. Extradimensional space has no vocabulary.

effects.target: Creates 1d4+2 shambling mounds with the advanced template. They willingly fight for you, carry out a specific mission, or act as bodyguards. Created for guard duty alone they instead last 7 months and can only be ordered to guard one site, and cannot move outside the spell's range measured from where each appeared. Only one shambler spell can be in effect at a time; casting it again dispels the earlier one. The shamblers have a shambling mound's fire resistance only if the ground where they appear is rainy, marshy or damp.

shambler.notes: Duration recorded as the ordinary 7 days. The alternative 7-month guard-duty duration is stated but the unit vocabulary has no month, and it applies only to a casting restricted to guarding one site - it is in the narrative text instead of being converted to a wrong number of days. The fire resistance belongs to the summoned creatures' own stat block, not to the spell, so it is not a resistance spec.

on_failure.target: The target sees its own clothing as humiliating and must spend a move action each round removing one worn item that a move action can remove, dropping it. Roll randomly among the belt, body, chest, eyes, feet, hands, head, headband, shoulders and wrists slots it actually has something in, ignoring items that take longer than a move action; it does not distinguish magical from mundane. It may take any other actions it likes. It regards the discarded items with revulsion, and if forced to touch one - for instance being struck with it as an improvised weapon - it is sickened for 1d3 rounds.

shamefully-overdressed.notes: The sickened 1d3 rounds is deliberately NOT an apply_condition: it fires only when someone forces the target to touch a discarded item, which may never happen. Emitting it would sicken every target on every casting.

effects.target: You take the form of a wide variety of creatures, the spell functioning as alter self, beast shape IV, elemental body IV, form of the dragon III, giant form II or plant shape III depending on the form chosen. You can change form once each round as a free action, immediately before or immediately after your regular action but never during it.

shapechange.notes: Polymorph: the statistics come from whichever polymorph spell the chosen form falls under, and change every round at will. Nothing fixed enough to convert.

effects.target: Changes a willing living creature you touch into an animal (as beast shape I), a humanoid (as alter self), or a monstrous humanoid (as monstrous physique I). The form cannot have a fly speed. Statistics change as the matching spell, except that the subject's ability scores and natural armour do not change. The subject can switch between its own form and the chosen one at will as a standard action.

shapechanger-s-gift.notes: The two exceptions (no ability score change, no natural armour change) are subtractions from another spell's effect, not effects of their own, so there is nothing to emit as a modifier.

effects.target: As shapechanger's gift, except the form may be an animal (beast shape I), elemental (elemental body I), fey (fey form I), humanoid (alter self), monstrous humanoid (monstrous physique I) or vermin (vermin shape I), and it may have a fly speed.

The targets count as mythic creatures for the purposes of path abilities, spells and any other effect that works differently on a mythic creature. It grants no mythic tiers and no uses of mythic power. You must be at least a 1st-tier mythic character to cast it.

share-glory.notes: One target per three caster levels. 'Counts as mythic' is a status the schema has no term for; it is not a permission, a bonus or a condition.

effects.target: May read, understand and speak one language you already know, chosen at casting - and one further language you know for every 5 caster levels, to a maximum of 5 at 20th level. The target must be physically able to produce the language's sounds or gestures to converse. A target without the mental capacity for language still understands and can carry out even complex instructions given in it, but gains no reasoning, so instructions must be free of ambiguity. It does not change the target's nature or its disposition toward anyone.

share-language.notes: The per-5-levels progression is real but counts languages, not dice; the scaling block only describes damage and healing dice, so it would have to be misread as one. Left in the permission text.

effects.target: As share language, but you divide the duration in 1-hour increments among the creatures touched: each recipient may read, understand and speak a language you know for as many whole hours of the 24 as you assign it.

share-language-communal.notes: 24 hours is the pool to be divided among targets, not the duration any one target gets. The duration schema cannot say 'divided among targets', so the division is stated in the effect text.

on_failure.target: Your mind links with the target's for a moment and a single memory of no more than 1 minute passes between you. You choose one of three: show the target one of your own memories, show the target one of its own memories, or view one of the target's memories.

effects.target: Your link with your familiar becomes a scrying sensor: you hear, see or smell (any one, your choice, changeable as a standard action) what your familiar experiences. You gain the benefit of any nonmagical special ability of your familiar tied to that sense, such as low-light vision or scent, but roll your own Perception. No line of sight or effect is needed, only an active empathic link. Magically or supernaturally enhanced senses do not work through it and you cannot see in darkness of any kind unless the familiar can. The link is detectable as a scrying sensor.

share-senses.notes: No sense spec: the senses gained are whichever ones the familiar happens to have, which is not knowable from the spell.

effects.target: As beast shape II, except you may only take the form of an animal of exactly the same kind as your animal companion or familiar. If your companion or familiar is not an animal, the spell does nothing.

The header reads 'hours/level (1) or until you return to your body' while the first line of the description reads 'Duration 1 minute/level or until you return to your body'. One of them is an erratum and the text does not say which; a 20-hour possession and a 20-minute possession are not the same spell, so no structured duration is asserted and the prose stays as printed.

The 'any creature' reading comes from the target line ('creature touched') against share skin's 'animal touched' - the description body of this entry is a bare cross-reference.

on_failure.target: A link forms between you and the target that carries pain the other way: you take only half the hit point damage from any effect or attack, and the target takes the other half. Harm that is not hit point damage - charms, ability damage, level drain, death effects - is not shared, and neither is a loss of hit points caused by a lowered Constitution score. When the spell ends damage stops being divided, but damage already shifted is not given back. The spell ends at once if you and the target move out of range of each other.

shared-sacrifice.notes: Halving incoming damage and redirecting the other half to a second creature is two things the vocabulary cannot say: damage_reduction is a flat subtraction, and no spec can name a different creature as the recipient. Emitting a damage spec here would deal damage to the wrong target, which is exactly the shield-other/thorn-body trap.

effects.target: Allies in range use one teamwork feat that you have, without needing to meet its prerequisites. At caster level 9th you may grant two of your teamwork feats, at 13th three, and at 17th four.

shared-training.notes: You plus one willing creature per three caster levels, none more than 30 feet apart. Which feat is granted depends on what the caster has, so nothing concrete can be emitted; the count progression is levels of feats, not dice, so it is not a scaling block.

effects.target: As wrath, except the bonuses against your designated foe are granted to one creature per caster level rather than to you alone, and every subject receives them against the same designated creature.

shared-wrath.notes: The bonuses themselves are stated only in wrath, which this entry does not reproduce. Writing numbers here would mean copying them from a spell outside this partition and outside this description - refused.

effects.target: Both creatures must be of the same gender. You take a negative level for the spell's duration; the other target gains a +1 insight bonus to caster level and a +1 insight bonus to the save DCs of all its spells. At 11th level you may instead take four negative levels for a +2 insight bonus, and at 17th six negative levels for +3. Anything that removes or prevents the negative level ends the spell immediately, and the negative levels vanish when it ends. Negative levels from multiple castings stack.

sharesister.notes: Deliberately not split into a combat_mod. The cost and the benefit land on two different creatures - the caster takes the negative level, the other target gets the bonus - and an effects list has no way to say which recipient a spec is for, so emitting the +1 would grant it to whoever the engine applied the spell to, including the caster. Also: 'insight bonus to caster level' is broader than the combat_target 'caster level checks', there is no target for spell save DCs, and negative level is not in the condition vocabulary. VOCABULARY GAP - per-recipient targeting, and negative levels.

Opponents still know which squares you occupy, so you cannot use this concealment for Stealth unless every square adjacent to you is at darkness or lower. shield-of-darkness.notes: Total concealment is a miss-chance rule with no spec; the schema has neither concealment nor a light level.

shield-of-fortification.notes: A percentage chance to cancel precision and critical damage. Not damage_reduction and not immunity - both would change the rule rather than express it.

Each warded creature also gains spell resistance 25 against chaotic spells and against spells cast by chaotic creatures, and is protected from possession and mental influence exactly as protection from chaos does it. If a chaotic creature succeeds at a melee attack against a warded creature, that attacker is slowed as the slow spell (Will negates, against this spell's save DC). Unlike protection from chaos, the AC and save bonuses apply against all attacks, not only those of chaotic creatures.

shield-of-law.notes: One creature per caster level in a 20-foot burst centred on you. The slow is RETRIBUTIVE - it lands on a chaotic attacker who hits a warded creature, not on the spell's subjects - so it is emphatically not an apply_condition here; that is the thorn body mistake. Spell resistance 25 has no spec: the vocabulary has combat_mod 'spell_resistance', but that is a bonus on checks made to overcome SR, the opposite side of the roll.

effects.target: Cast on a shield you are wielding, it fractures into two shards plus one more per 2 caster levels, to a maximum of 12 at 20th level. While it is active you lose the shield's bonus to AC as the pieces orbit you. On your turn you may direct the shards to attack an adjacent opponent as a move action; their attack bonus is your caster level plus the ability modifier that sets your spell save DCs, they deal 1d4 points of slashing and piercing damage plus 1 point per shard beyond the first, and they threaten a critical on 19-20. They count as magic weapons for bypassing damage reduction, and if the shield was of a special material such as adamantine the shards bypass DR and hardness as that material too. When the spell ends the shards reform into the shield and you regain its AC bonus if you have a free hand; otherwise it falls in your square.

shield-of-shards.notes: The 1d4 is not converted to a damage spec: it happens only on a later successful attack roll that the caster spends a move action to make, not when the spell is cast, and its size depends on a shard count that itself scales. Emitting it would deal 1d4 to something at casting. The lost shield bonus is also unconvertible - its size is whatever shield the caster happens to be carrying.

effects.target: A disk of sunlight forms on one arm. Any creature that strikes you with a melee attack deals its damage normally but itself takes 1d6 points of fire damage plus 1 point per caster level (maximum +15). A creature attacking you with a reach weapon takes none of it. The disk sheds light as a continual flame. Only one instance of this spell can be active at a time, and it does not stack with similar damaging aura spells such as fire shield.

shield-of-the-dawnflower.notes: RETRIBUTIVE - refused as a damage spec on purpose. The 1d6+1/level is taken by whoever hits the caster in melee, not by any target of the spell, and it fires on each such attack rather than on casting. This is the thorn body defect verbatim; a damage spec plus a per-level scaling block would look perfectly plausible here and would burn the wrong creature. Element already derived as fire.

effects.target: As the lesser spell: any creature striking you in melee deals normal damage but takes 1d6 points plus 1 point per caster level, half of it fire and half holy damage as flame strike. An undead creature, or one particularly vulnerable to light, takes 2d6 plus 1 point per caster level instead. Creatures using reach weapons take none of it. The disk sheds light as daylight. Only one instance can be active at a time and it does not stack with fire shield or with shield of the Dawnflower.

shield-of-the-dawnflower-greater.notes: Retributive, as the lesser spell - not converted to damage. Also note 'holy damage' is not in the damage_type vocabulary at all; the nearest is positive, which is a different rule. VOCABULARY GAP - retributive/aura damage has no home, and holy is not a damage type.

shield-of-wings.notes: The 50-foot fly speed is stated outright and is the state the spell starts in, so it is emitted. The fire resistance 30 and the fire immunity are NOT emitted as resistance/immunity specs: neither is granted on casting - each is bought by losing a wing, the resistance lasts only the remainder of that round, and the immunity only begins as the spell is expiring. Duration is 'minutes/level (see text)'; the 'see text' is the extra minute of immunity at the end, which cannot be added to a per-level duration. Element already derived as fire.

Harm that does not involve hit points - charm effects, temporary ability damage, level drain, death effects - is unaffected, and hit points lost to a reduced Constitution score are not split. shield-other.notes: The +1s are stated and land on the subject. The damage transfer moves half of the subject's incoming damage onto the caster; no spec can name a second recipient, and a damage spec here would deal damage to the subject rather than move it. Narrated.

effects.target: You and one creature within 10 feet may speak to each other without being overheard for as long as it stays within that distance. The conversation cannot be spied on, including by divination, and onlookers can tell you are talking but can neither read your lips nor hear you unless they are the spell's target. Speaking to anyone else is heard normally - only the exchange between you and the target is shielded - and it protects speech only, not writing, sign language or any other form of communication.

As shield speech, except every creature inside a 30-foot emanation centred on you may speak with every other creature inside it as though linked by shield speech. Anyone they speak to outside the area hears them normally.

Cast on a tribal standard or banner, the spell works as sanctuary for that object alone: any creature that is not a member of the tribe the standard represents must make a Will save to attack or even touch it. It also raises the standard's hardness by 2.

shield-the-banner.notes: '+10 to the standard's hit points for the duration' is read as 10 temporary hit points, which is what a hit point grant that expires is; the number is exact and not inferred. The +2 hardness has no spec - damage_reduction would be a different rule, since hardness applies to objects and is subtracted before DR.

effects.target: The target sounds as though it is somewhere else within range - its movements, its speech, every sound it makes. While you concentrate you can move the apparent source anywhere in range; once you stop, the sound keeps the same relative distance and direction from the target. It fools sound-based blindsense and blindsight, including echolocation, but not other forms of blindsense or blindsight, lifesense, normal vision or tremorsense. An unwilling target gets a save, and anyone interacting with the illusion gets a Will save to disbelieve.

shifted-steps.notes: Printed duration is 'concentration + 1 round/level'. Only the trailing per-level part is emitted, because the schema's kinds are exclusive and 'concentration' alone would throw away the rounds that run on after you stop. Element already derived as sonic.

effects.target: The earth or sand in the area churns, wiping out tracks and counting as difficult terrain. Acrobatics checks in the area take a penalty equal to your caster level, to a maximum of 10. A creature entangled here that tries to move must make a second Reflex save or fall prone. A creature with the stability racial trait, such as a dwarf, adds it as a bonus on these saves. As a move action you may slide the area up to 10 feet in any direction; entangled or prone creatures in it are carried along without provoking attacks of opportunity, as may unattended Medium or smaller objects, which can also end up shallowly buried.

shifting-sand.notes: The Acrobatics penalty is deliberately not a skill_mod: its size is the caster level (max 10), and skill_mod holds a fixed number, so any value written there would be right at exactly one caster level and wrong at every other. The prone follow-up is a second save contingent on the creature choosing to move, so it stays narrative rather than nesting as a certainty.

effects.target: Shadows wash over everyone in the emanation, blurring friend and foe. No one risks striking an ally, but every creature in the area may treat any other creature in the area as an allied threatening creature for flanking. Whenever a creature in the area provokes an attack of opportunity from an enemy, that enemy's allies in the area must succeed at a Reflex save or lose one attack of opportunity that round. It does not hinder precision-based attacks and creates no dim light. Creatures under true seeing are unaffected, as are creatures with scent or keen scent, blind creatures, and creatures that function without sight such as those with blindsight or blindsense.

shifting-shadows.notes: Flanking eligibility and attack-of-opportunity budget are not in the vocabulary at any level.

effects.target: One nonmagical object you touch, up to 2 cubic feet per caster level, shrinks to one-sixteenth of its size in every dimension - about 1/4,000 of its volume and mass, effectively four size categories smaller. You may optionally also make the shrunken object clothlike. It returns to normal size and composition when thrown against a solid surface or on a word of command from you, which ends the spell. Even a burning fire and its fuel can be shrunk. Made permanent with permanency, the object can be shrunk and expanded any number of times, but only by you.

shrink-item.notes: '(see text)' on the duration is the permanency option, which the schema cannot express as a conditional kind.

shroud-of-darkness.notes: One target per three caster levels, none more than 30 feet apart. Perceived light level has no spec; blinded would be a much harsher and different rule.

shroud-of-innocuity.notes: The +2 is written with no bonus type, so it is untyped - 1e's default for an unnamed bonus, not a choice made here. The qualifier lives in the note field, which is what render() reads it from.

effects.target: As entangle, except the plants are coated with an irritating sap that raises a painful, itching rash. A creature that enters the area or ends its turn in it must save against the sap each time.

sickening-entanglement.notes: The Reflex-partial entangling half belongs to entangle, which this description does not restate, so no numbers are copied in for it. Only the Fortitude/sickened half, which this spell states itself, is emitted.

effects.target: Disease suffuses you: any creature you hit with a melee attack must succeed at a Fortitude save or be sickened for 1 minute. A creature immune to disease is immune to this sickening.

sickening-strikes.notes: Not emitted as a save_gate with apply_condition, even though a save and a condition are both stated plainly. The spell's target is 'you' - it is a personal buff - and the sickening lands on whoever the caster later hits in melee, so a gated condition on this spell's target would sicken the caster. Same class of error as thorn body: the save and condition are real, the recipient is not the spell's target.

effects.target: Inanimate plants gain limited movement and a semblance of life: each targeted Large plant acts as a light catapult for the duration, using your caster level as its targeting bonus. You must spend a standard action to aim each tree before it first fires and again whenever you want it to fire at a new target, and a free action lets you order one or all of them to stop. They load themselves with rocks and boulders from the area, digging them out of the ground if need be, though you may supply ammunition instead. They will not load flaming ammunition and cannot be affected by energy siege shot if fire is the energy chosen.

siege-of-trees.notes: One plant per three caster levels. Siege engine damage belongs to the catapult's own entry, not to this spell, and it is dealt by an attack the caster aims later.

effects.target: As siege of trees, except you may affect Large, Huge or Gargantuan plant creatures, and each acts as a catapult of its own size.

You search one 10-foot cube within 30 feet at a distance as though examining it closely: make a Perception check at a -5 penalty, modified normally for conditions but with no penalty for distance, and compare it to the DC of any hidden feature such as a secret door, a trap or hidden treasure. You must be able to see the area, and you find only what sight or touch could reveal. It detects objects and features, never creatures.

sift.notes: The -5 is not a skill_mod: it modifies the one Perception check the spell itself makes, and a skill_mod would instead saddle the caster's own Perception with -5. The spell is instantaneous, so there is no window for a modifier to sit in at all.

effects.target: As message, except the only thing you can convey is that you are a worshipper of Sarenrae. Once told, the target may reply that it understands your sign. The spell carries meaning rather than sound and crosses any language barrier.

You teleport up to one willing ally per five caster levels to your location. You choose which allies at casting; each has 1 round to accept or refuse and teleports the instant it accepts, arriving in a puff of brimstone in a space adjacent to you as though you had cast teleport on it, with your location counting as at least 'studied carefully'. An ally arriving into a fight you are already in may roll initiative on arrival and is not flat-footed despite having taken no actions. The spell does not work in an area warded against intrusion by evil creatures, such as a magic circle against evil.

signifer-s-rally.notes: Teleportation - no spec. Note this is the spell family that produced the Teleport mishap-damage defect; there is no mishap table here and no number that could be mistaken for damage.

effects.target: As commune with nature, except it reveals up to three details about the territory you are standing in, chosen from bodies of water, features, minerals or plants. For each feature learned you also know which skills can be used to find it, and you gain 1d6 Discovery Points toward finding it.

signs-of-the-land.notes: 1d6 here is Discovery Points, a subsystem currency - not damage and not healing.

effects.target: sonic and language-based attacks, spells and effects
effects.note: while inside the area

effects.target: Complete silence fills a 20-foot-radius emanation. All sound stops: conversation is impossible, spells with verbal components cannot be cast, and no noise issues from, enters, or passes through the area. Cast on a point in space the effect is stationary; cast on a mobile object or a creature it moves with them. An unwilling creature may attempt a Will save to negate it and may use spell resistance. Items carried by a creature, and magic items that emit sound, get the benefit of those saves and that spell resistance; unattended objects and points in space do not.

silence.notes: The immunity is stated outright ('Creatures in an area of a silence spell are immune to sonic or language-based attacks, spells, and effects') and applies to everyone in the area, friend or foe. The silencing itself - no verbal components, no sound crossing the boundary - has no spec.

effects.target: Creates a visual illusion of an object, creature or force as you picture it, filling up to four 10-foot cubes plus one more per caster level and shapeable. It makes no sound, smell, texture or temperature. You can move the image within the limits of the effect's size. A creature that interacts with it may attempt a Will save to disbelieve.

Sounds and sonic effects originating inside a 5-foot-diameter emanation are muffled to anyone outside it: Perception DCs to hear or understand sound leaving the area go up by 20, and the save DCs of any such sonic effects go down by 2. Sounds entering the area are unaffected, as are the Perception checks of creatures inside it.

silent-table.notes: +20 and -2 modify a DC that other creatures roll against, not any statistic of a creature the spell is on. skill_mod and save_mod both modify the roller's own number, which is the opposite adjustment. VOCABULARY GAP - no way to shift a DC.

effects.note: only on rounds you choose to defend with the scarf rather than attack with it

effects.target: An ordinary scarf or similar garment gains the strength of steel with no change to its weight or flexibility. Each round on your turn you decide whether to defend with it, gaining the shield bonus, or to attack with it as though it were a whip.

silk-to-steel.notes: +2 shield bonus is stated with its type. It is not unconditional - it applies on rounds the caster chooses to defend - so the exclusivity is carried in the note field that render() prints as a qualifier. The whip attack is a granted attack, so its damage is the whip's, not the spell's.

effects.target: An illusory cloud of silt drifts with you in a 20-foot radius. Creatures inside it when it is cast, you included, have total concealment; creatures that move in afterwards get ordinary concealment instead. Everyone inside sees everyone else, and out of the cloud, as if it were transparent. If a creature other than you that has total concealment from the cloud attacks anyone, it drops to ordinary concealment; if you attack anyone, the spell ends. A creature outside that succeeds at a DC 20 Knowledge (nature) check notices the cloud is unnaturally compact and fast-moving and may immediately attempt a save to disbelieve, and circumstances such as the cloud hanging in otherwise clear water can change that DC. Can only be cast underwater.

silt-sphere.notes: Concealment and total concealment are miss-chance rules with no spec.

effects.target: As daylight, except the touched object sheds bright silvery light in a 20-foot radius and dim light out to 40 feet. The bright light hurts creatures susceptible to alchemical silver: a creature with DR/silver that begins its turn within 20 feet is automatically dazzled, and is also sickened unless it succeeds at a Fortitude save. Both wear off 1 round after it leaves the light, and a creature that leaves and returns must save again. Only creatures within the 20-foot bright radius are subject to this.

silverlight.notes: The dazzled and sickened conditions are real and plainly stated, but they are NOT emitted, because this spell's target is 'object touched' - a torch or a coin. Effects hung on that target would dazzle the object. The creatures who actually take them are third parties with DR/silver who begin a turn in the radius, which no spec can address. Same who-takes-it failure as sickening strikes.

effects.target: Creates a partially real duplicate of any creature, formed from ice or snow. It looks like the original but has only half its levels or Hit Dice, with the hit points, feats, skill ranks and special abilities of a creature of that level. You cannot duplicate a creature whose HD or levels exceed twice your caster level. Make a Disguise check when you cast it to set the quality of the likeness; someone who knows the original may see through it with a Perception check opposed by that Disguise check, or a DC 20 Sense Motive check. The simulacrum is always under your absolute command, though with no telepathic link you must issue orders some other way. It cannot gain levels or grow in ability, and at 0 hit points or otherwise destroyed it reverts to snow and melts away. Repairing damage to one takes at least 24 hours, 100 gp per hit point, and a fully equipped magical laboratory.

simulacrum.notes: Creation of a creature - no spec. The 100 gp/hit point is a repair cost, not healing.

effects.target: As simulacrum, except you cannot duplicate a creature whose HD or levels exceed your caster level, the duplicate has no magical abilities, and it is not under your control - though it knows you made it.

Touching a creature, you try to end one spell currently on it as though with a targeted dispel magic. Name a specific effect if you know it; otherwise the spell starts with the highest-level spell in effect and works down until it dispels one or runs out. If it ends one, that spell's remaining duration transfers to you and plays out as though you had been its original target. If the spell allowed a save to resist, you get that save as if it were being cast on you now - which does not reset its duration.

siphon-magic.notes: Dispelling and transferring another spell's remaining duration; spell_effect names a spell to act as, which is not the same thing, and the spell in question is unknown until play.

effects.target: You drain the target's might and hand it to someone else. The subject takes a penalty to Strength equal to 1d6 + 1 per two caster levels, to a maximum of 1d6 + 5, which cannot drop its Strength below 1; a successful Fortitude save halves the penalty. It does not stack with itself or with ray of enfeeblement's penalty. You may grant any one creature adjacent to you, including yourself, an enhancement bonus to Strength equal to the penalty imposed.

siphon-might.notes: Refused as ability_damage: this is a Strength *penalty* (it cannot reduce the score below 1, it does not stack with itself, and it is explicitly the ray of enfeeblement family), and ability damage is a different rule that heals at its own rate. ability_mod could carry a penalty but its amount is a flat integer and this one is 1d6 + half caster level. The matching Strength bonus also goes to a third creature the effects list cannot name. VOCABULARY GAP - a dice-valued ability penalty.

sirocco.notes: Fatigue is in BOTH branches on purpose: the save halves the fire damage rather than negating it, and the text keys fatigue to taking damage, so a creature that saves is still fatigued. Prone is only in the failure branch because the save explicitly negates it. The falling damage is not the spell's - it is fall damage taken by a third party who fails a Fly check - so it is narrated. AMBIGUITY FOR REVIEW: the description reads as a single blast, and is converted that way, but the fatigue clause refers to 'a previous round of exposure to a sirocco spell', which implies the cylinder damages creatures again each round it persists. Nothing in this text says 'each round', so no repeating application is asserted here. Element already derived as fire.

effects.target: Corpses you touch become 1 Hit Die skeletons that crew a ship and obey you. Each has a Profession (sailor) score equal to half your character level plus your Wisdom modifier (cleric), Intelligence modifier (witch or wizard) or Charisma modifier (sorcerer or summoner), and no other abilities: they cannot speak, attack, or even defend themselves, they are proficient with no weapon or armour, and the only orders they follow concern running a ship. A single casting cannot create more Hit Dice of crew than twice your caster level, a limit that desecrate doubles. They do not count against the total Hit Dice of undead you can control. Each must come from a mostly intact humanoid corpse with bones; any flesh left on the corpses melts away into fog as you cast.
ability or skill checks to read difficult or fragmented text quickly, and Research checks made in a library

You read written material in a quarter of the usual time. Combined with comprehend languages you read otherwise incomprehensible text four times faster than that spell allows. Where the text is fragmented, especially hard, or otherwise needs an ability or skill check such as Linguistics to read at all, the spell does not speed you up; it grants the bonus on that check instead.

skim.notes: +8 is written with no bonus type, so untyped. It is a situational_mod rather than a skill_mod because it does not attach to one named skill - it covers whichever ability or skill check the GM calls for to read the passage, plus Research, which is not in the skill vocabulary at all.

effects.target: A malign spirit is mixed into a piece of food, a drink, or any consumable item including alchemical items, potions and elixirs. The spell discharges when the item is consumed, taking hold of the consumer unless it succeeds at a Fortitude save. The spirit settles into that creature's skin as a painless knot of wrinkles and tags that looks vaguely like a face when it stirs, and you count as holding a body part of that creature for scrying and similar divinations. Once per day, as a standard action from up to a mile away, you can make its skin crawl: it is sickened for 1d4 rounds plus 1 round per two caster levels, to a maximum of 5 extra rounds at 10th level, unless it succeeds at a Fortitude save. Alternatively, once per day you may remotely use a hex, a mind-affecting spell, or a necromancy spell causing disease or possession on it. The haunt-like manifestation appears in whichever round you use either power.

skin-tag.notes: The sickening is real and its formula is exact, but it is not emitted: this spell's target is 'beverage or piece of food touched', so a condition on the target would sicken the drink. The creature that takes it is whoever later consumes the item, and it only happens if the caster spends a standard action on it, once a day, from up to a mile away. Printed duration is '1 day + 1 day/level'; the schema cannot add a fixed term to a per-level one, so only the per-level part is structured and the extra day is recorded here.

effects.target: Your skin peels away and animates as a creature you control, and you may move your consciousness between it and your body as a standard action. While your mind is in your body you are helpless except to transfer your will or dismiss the spell. The skin is identical to you except that it has half the hit points you had at casting and cannot be healed above that, has the construct type with its traits and immunities, Str 3, no Constitution, DR 10/piercing or slashing, and compression; it can take any action you could take in your own body, including casting spells. When the skin leaves, your body drops to 0 hit points, cannot heal naturally and cannot be cured by hit point healing - only regenerate, heal, a ring of regeneration or another effect that regrows limbs will restore your skin and let you heal above 0. If your body is regenerated before the skin returns, the skin dies and your consciousness snaps back. The skin can be preserved with gentle repose and serves for anything needing your flesh, such as resurrection. When it returns to you, you regain hit points equal to the skin's remaining hit points. If the spell ends before you are reunited, or the skin is killed while you are in your body, you stay helpless at 0 hit points until your body is fully restored. If your body dies while you inhabit the skin, you die when the spell ends whatever the skin's hit points. If body or skin is slain with your consciousness in it, the spell ends and you are killed instantly. Long scars are left where the skin split, and they fade normally with healing magic.

skinsend.notes: The hit point figures here describe the animated skin's own statistics, not damage or healing the spell deals to anyone; 'you regain hit points equal to the skin's remaining hit points' is a reunification bookkeeping step with no fixed value. Nothing convertible.

effects.target: The mount you are riding sprouts angelic wings and gains a fly speed equal to its own base speed, with average manoeuvrability. It also gains a bonus on Fly checks equal to your caster level.

sky-steed.notes: Neither number is a number. The fly speed is 'equal to its base speed', which depends on the mount, and the Fly bonus is the caster level. speed and skill_mod both take fixed integers, so either would have to be invented.

effects.target: May swim through the air. A target with a swim speed moves through air at that speed; otherwise it must make Swim checks to move as normal. Still air counts as calm water, light or moderate wind as rough water, strong or severe wind as stormy water, and it cannot swim through anything stronger. It does not grant the ability to breathe air to a creature that cannot.

sky-swim.notes: Not a speed spec: the movement rate is the target's own swim speed if it has one, and otherwise there is no rate at all, only Swim checks.

effects.target: You designate a hemisphere within range, up to four 10-foot cubes plus one per caster level and shapeable; solid objects such as a wall or ceiling make it conform to the geometry of the place instead. It shows the sky as it appears directly above where the spell was cast, seeing past rock, stone or anything else in the way. That image counts as the real sky for any effect requiring a view of the sky, sun, stars or similar features, including spell preparation and deific obediences, but it does not enable spells that draw power from the sky such as call lightning. The light it makes behaves normally and harms creatures vulnerable to bright light or direct sunlight.

Slapping or wounding a sleeper wakes it and normal noise does not; waking one is a standard action, an application of aid another. The spell does not target unconscious creatures, constructs or undead.

sleep.notes: Both conditions are stated - the slumber itself and 'Sleeping creatures are helpless'. The 4 HD budget and the targeting order have no spec; note that 4 HD is flat at every caster level, so there is deliberately no scaling block.

on_failure.target: An unconscious or sleeping creature rises and moves in a half-awake state. Led or guided it staggers along, but stays helpless for every other purpose: it moves at half speed, is limited to a single move action each round, cannot move faster or take any action but movement without magical help, and automatically fails Dexterity- and Strength-based skill checks. If it takes any damage it must save again or the spell ends and it wakes, provided it has more than 0 hit points. When the spell ends or is dismissed it is still unconscious and must be woken normally - the spell never wakes it, stabilises it, or heals it. A disabled creature moved this way does not start dying again from the movement.

sleepwalk.notes: Not converted to apply_condition helpless: the target is already unconscious and helpless before the spell is cast, so the spell does not inflict that - it preserves it while adding movement. Emitting it would record the spell as the source of a condition it did not cause.

effects.note: a creature that is already asleep gets no save at all

on_failure.target: The target rises from sleep as if sleepwalking and carries out a course of activity you describe in a sentence or two, taking effect at once if it is already asleep or as soon as it falls asleep if awake; you may tell it to wait before acting. The activity must not have it directly harm itself or others - unlocking doors and windows or poisoning an ally's rations is allowed, jumping off a roof or coup de gracing a sleeping ally is not - and an instruction that would cause direct harm wakes it just before the act, leaving it a vague memory of what it was meant to do. It moves at its own speed but cannot run or go faster, sees in the dark as though it had darkvision, and can do most simple and skill-based things, but cannot fight, cast spells, or do anything needing real cognition such as complex decisions, puzzles or complicated magic items. If it takes damage it saves again, and success ends the spell and wakes it. On finishing the task, or when the spell ends or is dismissed, it is still unconscious, returns to where it was sleeping, and must be woken normally, remembering nothing but the exception above. Unlike sleepwalk, this automatically fails on a creature unconscious for any reason other than sleep, and the target never knows it was programmed unless it was woken for being about to cause harm.

sleepwalking-suggestion.notes: 'Will negates or none (see text)' resolves to: no save while asleep, a save if awake. The gate is kept with that stated on it rather than dropped, since the save does exist for a conscious target.

effects.target: Driving sleet fills a 40-foot-radius, 20-foot-high cylinder, blocking all sight within it including darkvision, and ices the ground. A creature can walk within or through the area at half speed with a DC 10 Acrobatics check; failure means it cannot move at all that round, and failure by 5 or more means it falls. The sleet puts out torches and small fires.

sleet-storm.notes: No save, no damage and no condition is named - the blindness inside it is total obscurement of the area, not the blinded condition applied to a creature. Element already derived as cold.

effects.target: Every wall and ceiling in a 30-foot emanation is coated with a slick substance. The DC of all Climb checks on those surfaces rises by twice your caster level, to a maximum of +20, and no creature can take 10 on a Climb check while scaling them, even one with a climb speed or another ability that normally allows it. Magical walls and surfaces, such as the sides of a create pit, are unaffected.

slick-walls.notes: Raises a check's DC rather than modifying any creature's Climb bonus, and by an amount that is twice the caster level. A skill_mod of -20 would be both the wrong side of the roll and a number true at exactly one caster level.

slipstream.notes: Both numbers are stated outright. The downhill/uphill variation is a qualifier on the land speed rather than a separate effect, so it sits in the note.

Once it has taken 5 or more points of Constitution damage this way its skin falls off to bare the musculature: the Constitution damage stops, and instead it takes a -4 penalty on saving throws against disease, pain effects and poison, and on Charisma-based skill checks other than Intimidate and Use Magic Device. The skin regrows quickly - as soon as the Constitution damage is fully healed the skin is whole again and the penalties end.

slough.notes: The 1d4 Constitution damage is NOT emitted as an ability_damage spec: it repeats every round until 5 points have accumulated, and the vocabulary has no repeating application, so a single spec would resolve a multi-round drain as one roll. The -4 penalties are also not emitted - they begin only after that threshold is crossed, so on casting they are not yet true, and save_mod covers a whole save rather than 'saves against disease, pain and poison'. VOCABULARY GAP - repeating ability damage, and a threshold that switches one effect for another.

These bonuses do not stack with a paladin's smite.

smite-abomination.notes: Both bonuses are variables - an ability modifier and the caster level - and combat_mod holds a fixed integer, so neither can be written without inventing a value. They also apply only against one nominated creature, which combat_mod cannot qualify.

It cannot stop looking at itself in every reflective surface it can find - a mirror, a pool, a polished shield - and in any social situation it remarks on how attractive it is or how ugly someone else is beside it. smug-narcissism.notes: -2 on ALL skill checks, so it is a situational_mod rather than 35 skill_mod specs; skill_mod names exactly one skill. No bonus type given, so untyped.

effects.target: Ordinary pieces of wood become snakes that attack your foes at once, and while they remain in sight you direct them telepathically as a free action. Only wooden objects not in a creature's possession and not part of a larger structure or plant can be used. Each casting creates a number of snakes equal to your caster level, with the more powerful kinds costing more of that total: a venomous snake from a stick or piece of firewood counts as 1; a constrictor snake from a staff or tree branch counts as 2; an advanced venomous snake from a stick or firewood counts as 2; an advanced constrictor snake from a staff or branch counts as 3; an advanced giant venomous snake from a log or pile of debris counts as 4; and an advanced giant constrictor snake from a fallen tree or large pile of debris counts as 5.

snake-staff.notes: The snakes' bites and constriction are their own stat blocks' damage, not the spell's.

effects.target: As stone shape, but for snow: you form a mass of snow up to 5 cubic feet plus 1 cubic foot per caster level into any shape you like. Crude objects are possible, fine detail generally is not, but a successful Craft (weapons) check - made by you, at the moment of casting, against the DC listed for that skill - lets you shape a bladed weapon; a failed check still casts the spell but produces a malformed, useless weapon. Only weapons can be made this way, not precise tools or elaborate armour. The finished item hardens into super-hard ice with hardness 5 and 10 hit points per inch of thickness, and takes double damage from fire. Anyone wielding such a weapon takes a -2 penalty on attacks because it is slippery and unwieldy, but it deals 1 point of cold damage on top of its normal damage. It lasts 24 hours before melting into uselessness.

snow-shape.notes: The -2 attack penalty and the 1 point of cold damage belong to the ice weapon and fall on whoever wields it and whoever it hits - not on the spell's target, which is a mass of snow. The spell is instantaneous, so there is no duration for a modifier to occupy either.

effects.target: All natural, undressed earth or stone in the area softens, 10 feet square per caster level and 1 to 4 feet deep depending on how tough the ground is: wet earth becomes thick mud, dry earth becomes loose sand or dirt, and stone becomes soft clay that can be moulded or chopped. Magical, enchanted, dressed or worked stone is unaffected, as are earth and stone creatures. Loose dirt is less trouble than mud, but everyone in it moves at half speed and cannot run or charge across it. Clay does not hinder movement but lets characters cut, shape or excavate where they could not before. Cavern ceilings and vertical surfaces such as cliff faces can be softened even though dressed stone cannot, which usually brings down a moderate collapse or landslide - treat it as a cave-in with no bury zone. Softening the ground under a building settles it and does moderate structural damage, though most well-built structures are only damaged, not destroyed.

soften-earth-and-stone.notes: 'Caught for 1d2 rounds and unable to move, attack, or cast spells' is left narrative rather than mapped to a condition: paralyzed is the nearest name but it also sets Dexterity to 0 and makes the creature helpless, which this does not, and entangled is far weaker than being unable to act at all. Naming either would be inventing a rule.

effects.target: attack
