effects.target: As fog cloud, but thick enough to impede movement as well as sight: creatures move through it at half speed, the vapours prevent effective ranged weapon attacks except for magic rays and the like, and no creature can take a 5-foot step inside it. A creature or object falling into the fog is slowed, each 10 feet of vapour reducing the falling damage by 1d6. Solid fog and effects like it do not stack with each other for the slowed movement or the attack penalties. Only a severe wind of 31 mph or more disperses it, and that takes 1 round. Made permanent with permanency, a solid fog dispersed by wind reforms in 10 minutes.

solid-fog.notes: Both -2s are stated and land on creatures in the fog. They are untyped because no type is named, and the melee restriction is a note because combat_mod's target dropdown has no melee/ranged split. The 1d6 per 10 feet is a REDUCTION of falling damage, not damage the fog deals - the opposite sign - so it is narrated.

effects.target: A single musical note takes temporary physical form and hangs wherever you like within range, serving as a hook, a pulley, a door blocker or anything else you can think of. Its look follows your melody - spiked or smooth, simple or convoluted, any colours you like - but it is always about the size of your outstretched hand. It resists being moved but vanishes instantly if enough force or weight comes against it. It has an effective Strength of 10 + your caster level and cannot hold more than a heavy load for that Strength without vanishing. Any creature that wins an opposed Strength check against it, such as by shoving open a door it is holding shut, also makes it vanish. It can never do a creature real harm, and it disappears if successfully attacked (AC 10 + your Charisma modifier) or beaten by a combat maneuver such as bull rush (CMD 2 + your base attack bonus + your Charisma modifier). A creature blocked by the note simply fails to shift it and loses that action for the round.

solid-note.notes: Printed duration is 'concentration + 1 round/level'; only the per-level tail is structured, as with shifted steps. The spell explicitly 'can never deal actual harm to a creature', so nothing here is damage.

effects.target: ref
effects.note: for any creature that begins its turn burrowing in the area

on_failure.target: entangled

effects.target: The stone, dirt and other earth in the area packs tight. Burrowing creatures, including those using earth glide, treat it as difficult terrain. Tremorsense and similar senses do not work inside it. A creature with the earth mastery special ability, such as an earth elemental, doubles its bonus on attack and damage rolls for as long as both it and its target are touching the affected area.

solidify-earth.notes: Earth mastery doubles a bonus the creature already has, whose size is not knowable from here, so it is narrated rather than given a number.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The creature turns on its own side rather than its foes: each round, at the beginning of its turn, roll - there is a 50% chance it attacks the nearest target. A creature that does not attack its nearest neighbour acts normally that round. Those that are forced to attack their fellows use everything they have, choosing their deadliest spells and best tactics, but they will not harm a target that has fallen unconscious.

song-of-discord.notes: Confused is the obvious-looking condition and is deliberately not used: 1e's confused has its own d100 table with several outcomes, while this is a flat 50% to attack the nearest target and otherwise act normally. Element already derived as sonic.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: str
As song of discord, except the creature automatically attacks the nearest target each round rather than having a 50% chance to.

on_success.target: A creature that saves is still affected, but the whole effect lasts only 1 round.

song-of-discord-greater.notes: The save is 'Will partial', and the partial is explicitly a duration cut to 1 round rather than a lesser effect - so the success branch carries the same +4 morale Strength with a 1-round duration rather than nothing. +4 morale to Strength is stated with its bonus type.

effects.note: for as long as the bardic performance you are maintaining continues
+1 point per caster level, maximum +15; delivered when the performance ends or you change to a different one

effects.target: exhausted
fatigued
nauseated
paralyzed
sickened
stunned

You must already have a bardic performance running to cast this - it need not be singing despite the name. Up to 3 creatures affected by that performance are the targets. The fast healing lasts as long as the performance does; ending or changing the performance ends the fast healing and triggers the burst of healing and the cures.

song-of-kyonin.notes: Checked against the blaze of glory defect and it is the other way round: this really is healing - 'heal 1d8 points of damage + 1 point/caster level' - on the spell's own targets, at a stated moment. The six cures are listed by name and all six are in the condition vocabulary. Duration also ends early when the performance ends or changes, which the schema cannot express alongside a per-level term.

effects.target: a Perform check attempted in the same round you cast this spell

Uplifting music from Elysium, Heaven or Nirvana accompanies you. Cast in the same round you activate a bardic performance, that round does not count against your bardic performance rounds for the day. Cast in the same round you cast a spell with the sonic descriptor, that spell's save DC increases by 1.

songbird.notes: +3 is a situational_mod rather than a skill_mod on perform because it applies to exactly one check made in the round of casting, not to the skill for a duration. The +1 to a sonic spell's save DC modifies another spell's DC and has no spec.

effects.target: You and your equipment become semisolid sound while keeping your shape. You take no penalties for squeezing and move through spaces as though three size categories smaller. Once per round you may make a melee touch attack dealing 1d6 points of sonic damage + 1 point per caster level. You count as incorporeal, though you cannot pass through solid objects, and any nonmagical attack you make deals half damage - magical attacks are unaffected and your magic items and equipment work normally. You cannot enter an area of silence; if you are caught in one, you take 1d6 points of sonic damage per caster level of that silence spell in the round it is cast and again in every round you end your turn in its area, with a Fortitude save each round for half. If the spell ends while you are in a square a creature of your size could not normally occupy, you take 3d6 points of damage and are shunted to the nearest space you can occupy.

sonic-form.notes: Three separate numbers here look convertible and none of them is. The 1d6+1/level is a granted touch attack's damage, dealt to whoever you hit and only if you hit. The 1d6/level in a silence area is dealt TO YOU, by someone else's spell, repeating every round. The 3d6 is an end-of-duration mishap for finishing in an occupied square - the Teleport defect in a different costume. Element already derived as sonic.

effects.target: A sweeping rush of sound hurls creatures or objects away from you in a straight line, as the violent thrust version of telekinesis. You can throw one object or creature per caster level, to a maximum of 15, all of them within 10 feet of each other, for a total weight of up to 25 pounds per caster level to a maximum of 375 pounds at 15th level. To hurl something at a particular target you must make an attack roll for each item thrown, using your base attack bonus plus your Intelligence modifier if a wizard, or Charisma modifier if a bard or sorcerer. Hurled weapons deal their standard damage with no Strength bonus, and arrows or bolts used this way deal damage as daggers of their size; other objects deal from 1 point per 25 pounds for less dangerous things up to 1d6 per 25 pounds for hard, dense ones. Anything that misses lands in a square adjacent to the target. A creature light enough to be hurled gets a Will save and spell resistance to negate the effect, as does a creature whose held possessions are targeted, and a hurled creature thrown against a solid surface takes damage as if it had fallen 10 feet - 1d6 points.

sonic-thrust.notes: Every damage figure here is contingent and none is the spell's own: hurled weapons deal the weapon's damage, other objects deal an amount per 25 pounds that depends on what the GM says the object is, and the 1d6 is fall damage taken on impact with a surface. All of them also require an attack roll to land first. Element already derived as sonic.

effects.target: You calm the elemental spirit inside a construct, lowering its chance of going berserk by 1d4% per four caster levels, to a maximum of 5d4%. Cast on a construct that has already gone berserk, and if you are its master, you may immediately roll d% to end the berserk state: it returns to normal function and its berserk chance drops to 0%.

soothe-construct.notes: 1d4 here is a percentage point of a construct's berserk chance - not damage, not healing, not an ability score.

effects.note: only for a creature that begins its turn in or on the mud; this healing is not increased by effects that boost healing

effects.target: Water, earth, sand and dust thicken into a wet healing mud filling one 5-foot square per caster level. It is difficult terrain, and created in water it does not sink unless weighed down by more than 100 pounds per caster level. A creature that rests partly or wholly submerged in it for 1 full minute is also healed of 1d4 points of ability damage to one ability score of its choice; a creature can be healed of ability damage this way only once per day.

soothing-mud.notes: 'Restores 1 hit point each round a creature begins its turn in or on the mud' is fast healing 1 in everything but name, and fast_healing is the one spec in the vocabulary that means per-round restoration, so this is the rare repeating effect that CAN be expressed. The 1d4 ability healing is left narrative because ability_restore requires a named ability and this one is the recipient's choice - picking one would invent it.

effects.target: Several conditions the target is suffering are lessened by one step: nauseated becomes sickened, stunned becomes dazed, exhausted becomes fatigued, frightened becomes shaken, and paralyzed becomes staggered. The duration is unchanged - only the severity drops. It does nothing to any condition not on that list.

soothing-word.notes: Refused as remove_condition + apply_condition pairs. Emitting the five remove_conditions alone would CLEAR nauseated, stunned, exhausted, frightened and paralyzed outright, which is far stronger than the spell; pairing each with its lesser condition would inflict sickened, dazed, fatigued, shaken and staggered on a target that had none of them. The step-down is conditional on the target already having the greater condition, and nothing in the schema can say 'if X then replace with Y'. VOCABULARY GAP - conditional downgrade of a condition.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: shaken

sotto-voce.notes: About as clean as this partition gets: one save, one named condition, one stated length. Only affects a living humanoid of 4 or fewer Hit Dice, which the target line already carries. Element already derived as sonic.

effects.target: You draw the soul out of a newly dead body - dead no more than 1 round per caster level - and imprison it in a black sapphire. Once trapped, the soul cannot be returned by clone, raise dead, reincarnation, resurrection, true resurrection, or even miracle or wish. Only destroying the gem or dispelling the spell on it frees the soul, which is then still dead. The focus is a black sapphire worth at least 1,000 gp per Hit Die of the creature whose soul is bound; too cheap a gem shatters when the binding is attempted. Creatures have no concept of Hit Dice as such, but the value of gem needed for a particular individual can be researched.

soul-bind.notes: 1,000 gp per HD is a material component cost, not a mechanic on any creature.

effects.target: As the spell completion option of trap the soul, but only against bodiless souls such as incorporeal undead or a soul already held in a gem, and creatures whose substance is a physical incarnation of a soul such as a petitioner. It does not work on creatures merely formed from souls or planar material, which is most outsiders. Its main use is moving souls from one receptacle to another, but it can also capture vulnerable souls not bound to mortal flesh. Capturing a petitioner makes its physical body vanish, to reappear only when its soul is released from the receptacle.
saving throws against effects that would trap or redirect the target's soul, such as magic jar, soul bind and trap the soul, and against effects that would turn the target into an undead creature
May attempt a saving throw to negate such a soul-trapping or undead-transforming effect even when that effect does not normally allow one.

An ethereal vault briefly envelops the target. Cast on a living creature that then dies, the spell protects both its body and its spirit for the rest of the duration; cast on a corpse within 1 round of death, it protects body and soul both; cast later, only the body is protected. Any spellcaster who worships Abadar may learn and cast this as a 4th-level spell even if it is not normally on her list. It can be made permanent with permanency at a cost of 7,500 gp and a minimum caster level of 11th.

soul-vault.notes: +4 has no stated bonus type, so untyped. It is a situational_mod rather than three save_mods because it applies against a named class of effect rather than to Fortitude, Reflex or Will as such. 'Granted a save even if one is not normally allowed' is a rule being relaxed, which is exactly what permission is for.

effects.target: You learn what stage of judgment a given soul has reached, or its fate after judgment. You must either identify the soul unambiguously or use the skull of the body it left as a focus. A soul of a different alignment from yours may attempt a Will save to resist, as though it were still alive. If the subject is still alive, or its soul has been destroyed, the spell fails and tells you nothing. If the soul has not yet been judged, you get an estimate of its location - usually somewhere in the River of Souls or the Boneyard - which may help you travel to it in cases involving soul bind or a devourer's devour soul, though the spell's real purpose is to establish how long the subject has been dead and therefore what life-restoring magic is needed. If it has been judged, you learn instead which plane it was sent to as a petitioner and its general location there, such as 'Elysium, beneath the boughs of the Witchwood'.

Cast on the same plane where the soul's petitioner form now exists, it also guides you along the shortest, most direct physical route to that petitioner, as find the path - and in that case alone the spell lasts 1 hour per caster level.

soulseeker.notes: Printed duration is 'instantaneous or 1 hour/level'. Instantaneous is structured because it is the ordinary case; the hours-per-level branch applies only to the same-plane guidance, and is stated on the permission spec that describes that branch rather than being asserted as the spell's duration.

effects.target: Castable only if you have a familiar. Your soul goes into your familiar's body and your familiar's soul into yours, as though each of you possessed the other with magic jar. You cannot move your soul back and forth freely - choosing to return to your body is a standard action and ends the spell. If either body is killed, both spirits return to their original bodies, the spell ends, and the original owner of the slain body dies.

An invisible barrier surrounds you in a 5-foot emanation and moves with you, inhibiting one category of magic - choose arcane or divine when you cast it. It works as antimagic field, but suppresses only spells of the chosen type and the supernatural and spell-like class abilities of classes granting that type of spellcasting; magic items, other spell-like abilities and other supernatural abilities are untouched. While it is up, you must succeed at a concentration check against DC 20 + twice the spell's level to cast any spell at all, arcane or divine, and failing the check loses the spell as though you had cast it to no effect.

source-severance.notes: Suppressing a whole category of magic has no spec; suppress_condition covers named conditions only.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: An idea, concept or suspicion is planted in the subject's mind. It genuinely believes the idea is its own, but is under no compulsion to act on it. If the idea runs against the subject's normal thinking - a paladin thinking 'I should murder my friends' - it may suspect mind-altering magic. The idea must be clear enough to convey in one or two sentences. No common language is needed, but without one only the most rudimentary ideas can be sown.

sow-thought.notes: Explicitly not a compulsion to act, so no condition and no permission - the subject's behaviour is unchanged and only its beliefs are not.

effects.target: You make an unattended Fine flammable object catch fire, as though using flint and steel except that it works in any weather and takes far less time to ignite.

spark.notes: Deliberately no damage spec despite the fire descriptor and the Fortitude save: the spell only ignites an unattended Fine object and names no damage at all. Whatever the resulting fire does is ordinary burning, not this spell. Element already derived as fire.

effects.target: being turned into undead spawn if killed

The target resists energy drain and blood drain attacks made by undead. If the attacking undead's Hit Dice are less than or equal to your caster level, the drain simply has no effect. If they are greater, the undead must succeed at a Fortitude save against this spell's DC with each attack for the drain to do anything at all. The ward stops only the Constitution damage from blood drain and the negative levels from energy drain, not any other effect of those attacks.

spawn-ward.notes: The spawn immunity is unconditional and stated flatly ('cannot be made into undead spawn if killed while the spell is in effect'), so it is emitted. The drain protection is not: it is either total or a save, depending on a comparison between the attacker's Hit Dice and the caster level, and that comparison cannot be written into any spec. Note also that the Fortitude save here is rolled by the ATTACKER, not by the spell's target - a save_gate on this spell would put it on the wrong creature.

effects.target: May speak and understand one regional human language of your choice that you yourself know - Varisian, Taldane, Tien and the like - selected when you cast the spell. It cannot be a dead language such as Ancient Osiriani or Jistka. The target speaks it with a native accent.

speak-local-language.notes: As tongues but narrowed to one living regional human language. The spell imparts no knowledge of the culture behind the language and does not change the target's appearance.

effects.target: May ask questions of animals and receive answers from them.

The spell makes no animal friendlier than it already was. Wary, cunning animals tend to be terse and evasive, and stupid ones make inane comments. An animal that is friendly toward you may do you some favour or service.

speak-with-animals.notes: The narrative spec is kept alongside the permission because the disposition caveat is the mechanically load-bearing half - it is what stops the permission from reading as 'animals will help you'.

effects.target: will
effects.note: the corpse gets this save only if its alignment in life differed from yours

on_failure.target: The corpse answers your questions, one per two caster levels. Its knowledge is only what it knew in life, including the languages it spoke, and answers are brief, cryptic or repetitive - especially from something that would have opposed you while alive. It cannot answer anything about events after its own death.

on_success.target: The corpse resists: it may refuse to answer your questions outright, or try to deceive you using Bluff.

effects.target: You may cast this on a corpse dead for any length of time, but the body must be mostly intact to respond, and must at least have a mouth to speak at all; a damaged corpse may give partial or partially correct answers. A corpse subjected to speak with dead within the past week cannot be questioned again. The spell does nothing to a corpse that has been turned into an undead creature.

speak-with-dead.notes: Both branches carry real content, so on_success is not empty here: a successful save does not negate the spell, it lets the corpse lie or stay silent.

effects.target: will
effects.note: the haunt gets this save only if its alignment is more than one step from yours; a haunt's Will modifier is 3 + its CR

on_failure.target: The haunt answers your questions, one per two caster levels. It knows what its original creature knew in life, including languages, and often remembers the circumstance that created it (though from the victim's own perspective, so not necessarily objectively), what triggers it, and how it can be laid to rest. Answers are brief, cryptic or repetitive, particularly from an angry, vindictive haunt, and it cannot speak to anything that happened after it was created.

on_success.target: The haunt resists and may refuse to answer or try to deceive you with Bluff; a haunt's Bluff modifier equals its CR, minimum +0, or whatever the GM sets from the original victim.

effects.target: Your range must reach a square within 10 feet of the haunt's area, and you must already know the haunt is there - casting this does not trigger it. A neutral or good haunt might cooperate with similarly aligned creatures simply to end its own suffering. A haunt questioned this way within the past week cannot be questioned again. Unlike a corpse under speak with dead, a haunt wants to express itself, if only to share its pain or make mischief.

speak-with-haunt.notes: The save modifiers given (3 + CR for Will, CR for Bluff) belong to the haunt rolling against this spell, not to the caster, so they are recorded as notes rather than as save_mod specs.

effects.target: will
effects.note: the plane gets this save only if its alignment is at least one step from yours; a plane typically has +20 on Will saves and a demiplane +15, plus 2 if mildly aligned or 4 if strongly aligned or possessing the wild magic trait

on_failure.target: The sentient plane answers your questions, one per two caster levels.

on_success.target: The plane resists the spell and does not answer.

effects.target: You tap the awareness of a plane with a sentient structure; a tangible manifestation of it, such as the ground, must be within range when you cast. A plane questioned this way within the past week cannot be questioned again, and the spell simply fails if the plane has no sentient structure.
May communicate with normal plants and plant creatures, asking questions and receiving answers.

A normal plant senses very little, so it cannot give or recognise detailed descriptions of creatures, nor answer anything about events outside its immediate vicinity. The spell makes no plant creature friendlier or more cooperative than it already was: wary and cunning ones are terse and evasive, stupid ones make inane comments, and a friendly one may do you some favour or service.
will
effects.note: the soul saves as if it were still alive

on_failure.target: You commune with the soul of a dead creature, which can speak normally in any language it knew. Unlike speak with dead, you are not restricted to questions - you and the soul can hold an ordinary conversation. The soul is not undead and is not compelled to speak or to be truthful. It generally knows only what it knew in life, though a soul that stayed aware of its surroundings after death may know more.

effects.target: To cast this you must be at the soul's place of death or in the soul's presence - held in a receptacle, powering an intelligent magic item, or otherwise.
May converse with a body of standing or flowing fresh water at least as large as you are, as stone tell. Flowing water can generally speak about events upstream, but not about events downstream.
attack
effects.note: melee touch attack rolls for spells delivered through the hand

effects.target: A ghostly hand shaped from your life force materialises and moves as you wish, delivering your touch range spells at a distance. Casting it costs you 1d4 hit points, which return when the spell ends - even if dispelled, but not if the hand is destroyed - and can be healed normally in the meantime. Any touch range spell of 4th level or lower you cast while it lasts can be delivered by the hand, and attacking with it counts as an attack normally. The hand always strikes from your direction and cannot flank as a creature can. Once it delivers a spell, or leaves the spell's range or your sight, it returns to you and hovers. It is incorporeal and cannot be harmed by normal weapons, has improved evasion, your save bonuses, and AC 22 (+8 size, +4 natural armour), with your Intelligence modifier applying to its AC as though it were its Dexterity modifier. It has as many hit points as you lost creating it, 1 to 4.

spectral-hand.notes: The 1d4 is explicitly NOT a damage spec. It is a cost paid by the caster, it is refunded when the spell ends, and this spell has no creature target - a top-level damage spec would be dealt to whatever the caster aimed at, which is precisely the Teleport-mishap failure. The +2 is emitted because the caster is the unambiguous recipient of a hand made from their own life force, with the touch-attack restriction in the note; combat_mod's 'attack' target cannot narrow itself to melee touch attacks.

effects.target: the spectral saluqi's bay ability

Creates a spectral saluqi, an undead canine like an oversized hound with black fur, a grey ruff and tail and milky grey eyes. It shares your alignment, converses with you telepathically, can see and attack ethereal creatures, and otherwise has a yeth hound's statistics. It usually leaves no tracks, preferring to fly an inch above the ground. Its bite counts as aligned to any single alignment you possess for overcoming damage reduction.

spectral-saluqi.notes: The immunity to the hound's bay is stated flatly and lands on the caster, so it is emitted. The hound's bite damage is the yeth hound stat block's, not the spell's.

effects.target: You summon a spectral creature shaped like any Tiny or smaller animal you choose, appearing in your square and glowing faintly in a colour you pick at casting, shedding light as a candle. It has the statistics of the animal it copies - ability scores, Armour Class, feats, senses, skills and speed - but is incorporeal and has only 1 hit point. It cannot attack, but follows any basic instruction you could give a pet or animal companion of similar intelligence, with no Handle Animal checks needed. It can speak with you but cannot be understood by anyone else, and it relays anything it directly witnessed with perfect clarity - sights, sounds and smells - without being able to interpret it. It can tell you how many people it saw, which way they went and what they carried; it cannot tell you whether they were friend or foe, or what they wanted.

spectral-scout.notes: Range is 1 mile - the scout's useful working distance rather than a targeting range.

effects.target: May read the lips of any creature within 100 feet that you can see and that is speaking a language you understand, with perfect accuracy.
other Perception checks made while reading lips, which takes moderate concentration

Lip-reading this way gives the exact wording of a conversation but does not help decipher obfuscated meaning such as secret messages or slang. It can be made permanent with permanency cast by a caster of 9th level or higher, at a cost of 2,500 gp.

speechreader-s-sight.notes: -4 is written with no bonus type, so untyped, and it is a situational_mod rather than a skill_mod on perception because it applies only while the caster is actively reading lips, not to Perception for the whole duration.

effects.target: If you successfully counterspell a spell of 3rd level or lower while this is running, whether through dispel magic or by ordinary counterspelling, you absorb the countered spell and use it to recover magic you have already spent. A wizard regains the use of any single spell cast since last preparing spells; a sorcerer regains a single spell slot. The spell or slot recovered must be of a level equal to or lower than the spell you counterspelled.

spell-absorption.notes: Recovering an expended spell or slot has no spec; spell_effect names a spell to act as, which is a different thing.

effects.target: As spell absorption, except you can absorb countered spells of 6th level or lower rather than 3rd.
will

on_failure.target: You learn some of the spells the target knows or has prepared - a number equal to your caster level. The lowest-level spells come first, ignoring 0-level spells, in random order: once all its 1st-level spells are revealed it moves to 2nd, then 3rd. It never reveals spells of 4th level or higher, nor spell-like or other special abilities.

effects.target: The spell does nothing at all against a creature that is not a spellcaster, that has only 0-level spells or spells of 4th level and higher prepared, that has spent all its spells, or that prepared none that day.

spell-gauge.notes: The number revealed scales with caster level, but it counts spells learned rather than dice, so it is not a scaling block.

effects.target: one specified spell of 4th level or lower per four caster levels, each named when this spell is cast

Against the named spells the warded creature effectively has unbeatable spell resistance - which naturally means it is no protection against spells that spell resistance does not apply to. It works against spells, the spell-like effects of magic items, and creatures' innate spell-like abilities, but not against supernatural or extraordinary abilities such as breath weapons or gaze attacks. Only a specific named spell can be warded against, never a domain, a school, or a group of similar spells. A creature can have only one spell immunity or greater spell immunity on it at a time.

spell-immunity.notes: immunity takes free text, so the class of protection can be stated exactly even though which spells are named is a decision made at casting.

effects.target: one specified spell of 4th level or lower per four caster levels, each named when this spell is cast
As spell immunity, except you divide the duration in 10-minute intervals among the creatures touched.

spell-immunity-communal.notes: The duration is a pool split among the recipients in 10-minute blocks, not the time each one gets; the schema cannot say 'divided among targets', so the division is stated in the narrative spec.

effects.target: one specified spell of 8th level or lower per four caster levels, each named when this spell is cast
As spell immunity, except the immunity extends to spells of 8th level or lower. A creature can have only one spell immunity or greater spell immunity on it at a time.

spell-immunity-greater.notes: The one-per-four-caster-levels count is inherited from spell immunity, which this entry defers to; only the level ceiling changes.

effects.target: one specified spell of 8th level or lower per four caster levels, each named when this spell is cast
As greater spell immunity, except you divide the duration in 10-minute intervals among the creatures touched.

spell-immunity-greater-communal.notes: Duration is a divisible pool, as with the other communal spells in this partition.

effects.target: The target gains spell resistance equal to 12 + your caster level.

spell-resistance.notes: The whole spell is one number and it still cannot be written. There is no spec that grants spell resistance: combat_mod's 'spell_resistance' target is a bonus on checks made to OVERCOME spell resistance, which is the attacker's side of the roll and the opposite of this. The value is also caster-level dependent, so no fixed integer would be right. VOCABULARY GAP - granting spell resistance, and the same gap seen on shield of law.

effects.target: will
effects.note: only if the target is currently under at least one harmless spell or effect

on_failure.target: Every harmless spell and effect currently on the target ends, stripping it of all of those benefits at once.

effects.target: A whip of cracking bluish-purple energy appears in your hand and lashes the protective magic off an enemy spellcaster. If the target is not under the effect of at least one harmless spell when you cast this, it is instead confused for 1d4 rounds.

spell-scourge.notes: Confused is deliberately not an apply_condition. It is the alternative branch, reached only when the target has no harmless spell on it to strip, so an unconditional condition spec would confuse every target - including the buffed ones the spell is actually meant for, who should be stripped instead. Printed duration is 'instantaneous or 1d4 rounds (see text)'; instantaneous is structured because that is the stripping branch, and the 1d4 rounds belongs to the confusion alternative.

effects.target: Spells and spell-like effects targeted on you are turned back on the caster who sent them. Only spells that take you as a target are turned - effect and area spells are not, and touch range spells are not stopped either. From seven to ten spell levels are affected, 1d4+6, rolled secretly. When a spell of higher level arrives than the turning you have left, it is partially turned: subtract the turning remaining from the incoming spell's level and divide by that spell's level to find what fraction gets through. For a damaging spell, you and the caster each take that fraction of the damage; for a nondamaging one, each of you has a proportional chance of being the one affected. If you and a spellcasting attacker both have spell turning running, a resonating field forms and the result is rolled randomly: 01-70 the spell drains away with no effect; 71-80 it affects both of you equally at full effect; 81-97 both turning effects stop working for 1d4 minutes; 98-100 both of you fall through a rift into another plane.

spell-turning.notes: Printed duration is 'until expended or 10 minutes/level'. The timed term is structured because it is the one the engine can count down; the discharge condition - the 1d4+6 spell levels being used up - is stated in the effect text, since until_discharged would throw the clock away and the schema cannot hold both. The d% table is a resonating-field MISHAP table and none of it is converted: 'affects both of you equally' and the planar rift are outcomes rolled between two casters, not effects this spell deals to a target.

effects.target: As lesser spellcasting contract, except that if the target has 9 Hit Dice or more you may imbue him with one or two 2nd-level spells and one 3rd-level spell.

spellcasting-contract.notes: Printed duration is 'permanent until contractually terminated' - permanent with a narrative escape clause the schema has no kind for. The imbued spells' identities are chosen at casting and the base mechanics live in lesser spellcasting contract, which this description does not restate, so no numbers are copied in.
